name: Russian Federation

summary.text: The Russian Federation appears on this site through the Trump Tower Moscow episode. The Special Counsel's report records that candidate Trump signed a letter of intent for a Moscow tower by November 2015, that Michael Cohen emailed and spoke with the office of the Russian government's press secretary Dmitry Peskov about the project in January 2016, and that the Trump Organization pursued it through at least June 2016. Separately, the Russian government's Federal Customs Service sued the Bank of New York in Moscow in 2007 over the 1990s Benex accounts, settling in 2009, and the U.S. government's 1990s assistance programme, reviewed by the GAO in 1996, supported Russian reformers around Anatoly Chubais.

facts.claim: Press accounts of Cohen's 2017 statement to Congress said Trump signed a nonbinding letter of intent with the Moscow developer I.C. Expert Investment Co. on 28 October 2015, that Felix Sater was brokering the deal, and that Cohen emailed Peskov after Sater suggested the proposal would require approvals within the Russian government.
facts.quote: Trump ultimately signed a nonbinding letter of intent with a Moscow-based developer, I.C. Expert Investment Co., on Oct. 28, 2015

facts.claim: The criminal information against Michael Cohen states that in August 2017 he sent a two-page letter to the Senate and House intelligence committees saying the Moscow proposal was not feasible and that he never agreed to travel to Russia, and alleges these representations were knowingly false.

facts.claim: The Russian government's Federal Customs Service sued the Bank of New York in Moscow beginning in May 2007 for $22.5 billion under the U.S. RICO statute's treble-damages provision; Finance Minister Alexei Kudrin later said the suit would be settled with the bank paying at least $14 million in court costs.
facts.quote: The Federal Customs Service sought $22.5 billion from the bank beginning in May 2007

facts.claim: The GAO reported in November 1996 that USAID, lacking the contacts and expertise for transition assistance to Russia, turned to private organisations including the Harvard Institute for International Development to provide direct technical help to Russian reformers, and that HIID was also expected to help oversee U.S. contractors.
facts.quote: USAID, the lead U.S. agency to provide transition assistance, lacked the contacts and expertise to accomplish this unprecedented task.

openQuestions: Site claim tested: 'a Moscow letter of intent signed mid-campaign' — supported by the Special Counsel's report (letter of intent signed by November 2015; project pursued through June 2016).

The site's Sater dossier links Sater to the letter of intent; the justice.gov results opened did not mention Sater by name, and the Sater brokering role rests here on press accounts of Cohen's statement.
No source was found stating that the Russian government itself approved or financed the Trump Tower Moscow project; Cohen's statement said he recalled no response from Peskov's office.
